page: Vultr vx1-m-32c-256g-1920s is a memory-optimized server instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 32 shared vCPUs, derived from 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 1920 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU hardware is included.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities across memory and processing workloads. The instance achieves top-tier status in memory write bandwidth for large blocks at 193.78 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression at 40.79 GB/sec. Passmark memory testing places the system in the top 10% with a score of 2989.67. Single-core CPU performance is strong, scoring 3055.98 in stress-ng, while multi-core performance is average at 48974.13, reflecting the shared CPU allocation tradeoff.

This hardware profile offers high resource density, particularly in memory capacity and local NVMe storage, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. Database operations perform strongly, as evidenced by a Passmark database score of 22098.23 and 63.9 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. It is highly suitable for large-scale databases, in-memory caching, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
